name: Arrhenius Reaction Rate
description: Compute the Arrhenius reaction rate k = A·exp(-Ea / (R·T)) where Ea is activation energy (J/mol), T is temperature (K), and R = NA·k_B is the gas constant built from CODATA constants. This model sits at the PhysTrix-ChemTrix boundary: T comes from a physical model (e.g. a diffusion sim), Ea is a property of a specific chemical reaction. The SI_ARRHENIUS tile handles the exponential via a preloaded LUT approximation. SI_CHECK enforces [k] = s⁻¹ (first-order) before output.
author: system

pipeline.note: R = N_A × k_B = 8.31446 J/mol/K (computed from CODATA, not hardcoded)
Dimensional check: result unit must be s⁻¹

validation: Ea=50 kJ/mol, A=10¹³ s⁻¹: k(300K) ≈ 1.0×10⁴ s⁻¹, k(600K) ≈ 2.7×10⁸ s⁻¹. Rate doubles for every ~10K near room temperature for typical Ea.
